title: Wish
description: One thing a person is looking for, or one thing they can offer to others, in their own words, on their OWN vault. ONE ENVELOPE PER WISH, NOT ONE PER LIST, and the reasons are mechanical: each wish has its own life (withdrawn, fulfilled, expired), each has its own AUDIENCE ('I am looking for a co-investor' and 'I am looking for people to play World of Tanks with' are shown to different people, and an envelope carries one ACL), and an eVault update replaces a sent array whole, so editing one line of a list-shaped record would rewrite every other line and oblige every writer to rebuild the list from a full read. What a person experiences as 'my wishlist' is the set of their Wish envelopes that are not withdrawn. THE TEXT IS VERBATIM: what the person wrote, never a summary, a translation or a tidied rewrite. An application that derives topics, keywords or matches from it keeps those derivations in its own storage; they are its inference, not the person's statement, and are never written into this record. A wish MAY POINT AT THINGS — the conference it is about, a person, an organisation, a talk, any envelope — through `about`, and may be about nothing in particular. A wish about a conference is still the person's wish and lives on their vault, not on the organiser's. Checked before minting (2026-11-15): no type for wishes, needs, offers, interests or 'looking for' exists in the central registry, in any platform's declaration, or as field names in any live record.

id.description: Stable application id for this wish, unchanged across updates. Distinct from the meta envelope id.

kind.description: What sort of wish this is. Free text with a DECLARED VOCABULARY rather than an enum, so that a new word costs no pull request: `seek` — something or someone the person is looking for (a contact, a skill, a fellow enthusiast, a piece of knowledge); `offer` — something the person can give others (expertise, a product, an introduction, help). A reader that meets a value it does not know MUST show the wish with that word as it is, and must not drop the record.

text.description: The wish, verbatim, in whatever language the person wrote it. One line of what they typed. Never rewritten by an application.

about.description: What this wish refers to, as an array of STRINGS, never objects: an object inside an array is split by a patch, a string cannot be. Three forms, told apart by their prefix: `w3ds://envelope?id=@<vault>/<metaEnvelopeId>` — an envelope, in the form the registered `Relation` ontology documents for `object` (the vault and the envelope id together, because an id alone addresses nothing); `@<uuid>` — an identity (a person, an organisation) by eName; `https://…` — something outside W3DS, such as the public page of an event that is not on any vault yet. A reader that cannot resolve an entry shows the wish anyway. Empty or absent means the wish is about nothing in particular — which is a statement, not missing data: 'I would like to meet people who play World of Tanks' applies wherever its author goes.

audience.description: Who the author meant this wish to be shown to, in words, because the ACL that enforces it is stripped from reads and a reader cannot see it. Declared vocabulary: `event` — people at the events named in `about`; `introductions` — anyone the capturing application may introduce the author to, at any event; `self` — nobody but the author; an application may use it to advise the author, and must never show it or quote it to anybody else. Unknown value: treat as `self`.

authorEName.description: Whose wish this is. Always the owner of the vault the record is on.

capturedBy.description: The eName of the application that recorded it, when it has one. Absent rather than wrong.

provenance.description: Where this record came from, in the shape the ecosystem already uses ({app, auto, generatedAt}, after Meshenger). `auto: false` says a person typed the text rather than an application composing it for them.

withdrawnAt.description: When the author took this wish back. There is no delete in this ecosystem, so removal is recorded: a reader must not show or match a withdrawn wish. Editing the words of a wish is recorded as withdrawing the old one and creating a new one, because a match made against the old words is not a match against the new.

fulfilledAt.description: When the author said this wish came true. Not written by crEVENTials yet; declared so that the first application to write it does not invent a second name.

expiresAt.description: After this instant the wish no longer applies. Not written by crEVENTials yet.
